title: Interference and audio problems
blurb: The big idea before the cards.

lines.caption: Fixing radio trouble is like being a doctor. Find the symptom, then the cause, then the cure.
lines.label: symptom, cause, cure

lines.caption: On FM, talking too loud or too close to the microphone makes your signal swing too wide. The cure is to back away from the microphone.
lines.label: back off the mic

lines.caption: If your own radio signal sneaks back along the microphone cable, your voice distorts. A clip-on ferrite choke stops it.
lines.label: choke the cable

lines.caption: Harmonics, spurious emissions and fundamental overload can all cause interference to other radios.
lines.label: three causes

lines.caption: When a strong, clean signal overloads a receiver, the cure is a filter at that receiver, such as a band-reject filter.
lines.label: filter at the receiver

lines.caption: And when a neighbor reports interference, check your own station first.
lines.label: start at home
